**TITLE II — DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES (cont.)**

**Office of the Secretary — General Departmental Management (cont.)**
- Appropriates $402,341,000 (plus $58,028,000 from PHS Act §241) for specified activities (PHS Act §229, U.S.-Mexico Border Health Commission, SSA §1110 research).
- $28,000,000 set aside for minority AIDS prevention/treatment.
- $40,000,000 for competitive sexual risk avoidance grants (defined as voluntarily refraining from non-marital sexual activity); requires medically accurate, evidence-based approach; teaches self-regulation, healthy relationships, resisting coercion; prohibits normalizing teen sexual activity; caps technical assistance/admin at 10%.
- Embryo adoption funds may cover medical/administrative services for adopting individuals, consistent with 42 CFR 59.5(a)(4).
- $5,000,000 for prize competitions (15 U.S.C. 3719) to accelerate kidney disease innovation.

**Medicare Hearings and Appeals**
- $196,000,000 (from Federal Hospital Insurance & Federal Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Funds); $40,000,000 available until Sept 30, 2025.

**Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology**
- $56,238,000 from PHS Act §241 for interoperable health IT.

**Office of Inspector General**
- $80,000,000; includes protective services for the Secretary and investigating child support non-payment (18 U.S.C. 228) and PHS Act §3022 (42 U.S.C. 300jj-52) activities.

**Office for Civil Rights**
- $32,000,000.

**Retirement Pay and Medical Benefits for Commissioned Officers**
- Such sums as may be required.

**General Provisions (TITLE II)**
- **Sec. 201:** Up to $50,000 for official reception/representation expenses with Secretary approval.
- **Sec. 202:** Caps extramural grant salary at Executive Level II; NIH may pay up to 100% of that rate.
- **Sec. 203:** No PHS Act §241 expenditures except as specifically provided, until Secretary reports planned uses to Appropriations Committees.
- **Sec. 204:** Up to 2.5% of PHS Act program funds available for evaluation (directly or by grant/contract), notwithstanding §241(a).
- **Sec. 205:** Up to 1% of discretionary HHS funds transferable between appropriations; no single appropriation increased >3%; no new programs; 15-day advance notice to Committees.
- **Sec. 206:** Modifies PHS Act §338E(c)(2) termination timeframe: up to 60 days after FY2024 contract award under §338B, or anytime if no funds received.
- **Sec. 207:** Title X funds barred unless applicant certifies it encourages family participation in minors’ decisions and counsels on resisting sexual coercion.
- **Sec. 208:** Title X providers not exempt from state child abuse/sexual abuse reporting laws.
- **Sec. 209:** Bars Medicare Advantage program funds if Secretary denies participation to an entity that refuses to cover/refer for abortions; requires actuarially sound capitation adjustments; entity must inform enrollees about Medicare-covered services.
- **Sec. 210:** No funds to advocate or promote gun control.
- **Sec. 211:** Up to 60 PHS employees assignable to child survival/AIDS programs via USAID, UNICEF, or WHO.
- **Sec. 212:** Authorizes Secretary for international health activities: (1) authority equivalent to State Department Basic Authorities Act §2(c); (2) advance/reimbursement to State for overseas facilities; grants/cooperative agreements for facilities abroad; (3) allowances/benefits similar to Foreign Service Act chapter 9 and locality pay up to DC rate.
- **Sec. 213:** NIH Director & OAR Director may transfer up to 3% of HIV research funds among institutes/centers; 15-day notice.
- **Sec. 214:** HIV research funds transferred to “Office of AIDS Research” account; OAR Director transfers amounts per PHS Act §2353(d)(3).
- **Sec. 215:** NIH Director may use PHS Act §402(b)(12) funds for transactions (other than contracts/grants/cooperative agreements) for research; peer review procedures at Director’s discretion, in lieu of specified PHS Act peer review sections.
- **Sec. 216:** Up to $100,000,000 for NIH facility alteration/repair/improvement; cap $5,000,000 per project.
- **Sec. 217:** 1% of NIH NRSA funds to HRSA Administrator for primary medical care research awards (PHS Act §§736, 739, 747 entities); 1% to AHRQ Director for health service research NRSA awards.
- **Sec. 218:** BARDA may enter multi-year contracts (up to 10 program years) for research services/security countermeasures if funds obligated for full period/termination costs and Secretary determines best interest; must include termination clause (41 U.S.C. 3903(c)) and congressional notice (41 U.S.C. 3903(d)).
- **Sec. 219:** Secretary must publish in FY2025 budget justification and website: FTE employees/contractors implementing ACA, by fiscal year since enactment, with program/funding details; may exclude certain employees (pre-ACA programs, <50% time on ACA, fixed-price contracts).
- **Sec. 220:** FY2025 budget must detail CMS Health Insurance Exchange funds by activity since ACA enactment.
- **Sec. 221:** No funds from Hospital Insurance or Supplemental Medical Insurance Trust Funds for ACA §1342(b)(1) risk corridors payments.
- **Sec. 222:** Within 45 days, Secretary transfers ACA §4002 funds per committee report; no further transfers; PHS Act §2821 funds available without regard to §2821(b).
- **Sec. 223:** Effective Nov 1, 2015–Jan 1, 2025, breast cancer screening recommendations administered as if referencing pre-2009 USPSTF recommendations, applying to all mammography modalities under SSA §1861(jj).
- **Sec. 224:** NIH Director may transfer opioid/pain/addiction funds among Institutes/Centers; 15-day notice; additional transfer authority.
- **Sec. 225:** Secretary must provide monthly Exchange enrollment figures and notify of new/competitive §330 grant awards; 2 business days’ advance notice before public release.
- **Sec. 226:** Biannual staffing report due 30 days after enactment.
- **Sec. 227:** HHS salary/expense funds available for employee/family travel for medical care when assigned to a public health emergency location (PHS Act §319) in U.S. or territory.
- **Sec. 228:** HHS may accept private donations for care of unaccompanied alien children (6 U.S.C. 279(g)(2)), including medical goods, school supplies, toys, clothing.
- **Sec. 229:** No Refugee and Entrant Assistance funds for unlicensed facilities housing unaccompanied alien children, except temporarily due to influx/emergency, subject to: (1) compliance with Flores Exhibit 1 requirements and staffing ratios (1:8 waking, 1:16 sleeping) after 6 months; (2) 60-day waiver for good-faith progress; (3) max 4 consecutive waivers; (4) ORR monitoring per Guide §5.5; (5) quarterly monitoring visits after 3 months; (6) ORR briefing to Committees within 60 days on influx facility requirements.
- **Sec. 230:** 15-day advance notice before operationalizing unlicensed facility; specify hard/soft-sided; provide analysis of necessity; within 60 days and monthly, report on children in care, length of stay, reasons for delay.
- **Sec. 231:** No funds to prevent Congressional oversight visits to unaccompanied alien children facilities, with 2 business days’ advance coordination.
- **Sec. 232:** Within 14 days of enactment and monthly, report on children separated by DHS, subsequently classified as UAC and transferred to ORR: number/ages, sector, documented cause of separation.
- **Sec. 233:** CDC salary/expense funds available for dependents’ schooling in U.S. territories, costs not exceeding DoD rates.
- **Sec. 234:** Amends PHS Act §231 (42 U.S.C. 247d-4a) Reserve Fund notification: requires 15-day advance notice with spend plan; quarterly updates; monthly reports on obligations >$5,000,000 and unobligated balances.
- **Sec. 235:** Amends CARES Act Title VIII CDC heading: strikes 14-day reporting requirement on Reserve Fund.
- **Sec. 236:** Rescinds $1,000,000,000 from “Nonrecurring Expenses Fund” by Sept 30, 2024; Secretary may transfer up to $85,000,000 to CDC Buildings and Facilities; restricts new obligations without prior notification; allows transfers into Fund.
- **Sec. 237:** Requires Secretary to submit report by March 16, 2023, and every 30 days, on expenditures under covered laws (Inflation Reduction Act §11004, ARPA, specified CARES/PPP/CRRSAA paragraphs): total obligated, list of awards/recipients, FTEs hired, unobligated funds, contractors, returned funds, transferred funds.
- **Sec. 238:** No General Departmental Management funds for employee travel.
- **Sec. 239:** No funds for research using human fetal tissue from induced abortion.
- **Sec. 240:** No funds to any “prohibited entity” (501(c)(3) essential community provider primarily engaged in family planning/reproductive health that performs or funds abortions, except rape/incest/life endangerment, and received >$23,000,000 in Title X FY2016); prohibition ends if entity certifies cessation; Secretary shall seek repayment for false certification.
- **Sec. 241:** No funds to support, administer, or issue grants promoting or facilitating abortion.
- **Sec. 242:** No Federal funding to EcoHealth Alliance, Inc. (New York).
- **Sec. 243:** No funds to enforce CMS “Omnibus COVID-19 Health Care Staff Vaccination” rule (Nov 5, 2021) or similar.
- **Sec. 244:** No funds to implement/enforce Executive Order 13988 (Preventing Discrimination on Basis of Gender Identity/Sexual Orientation).
- **Sec. 245:** Starting 4th day after enactment, General Departmental Management appropriation reduced by $1,000/day until FY2023/2024 Moyer Report submitted.
- **Sec. 246:** No funds to require Title X projects to refer for abortions; no provider required to subvert state law limiting abortion referral/counseling.
- **Sec. 247:** Amends PHS Act Title II, inserting §245A: Civil action for designated violations (violation of §507(d) of Div. H, Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023, or funding conditions thereunder); qualified parties (U.S. AG, state AG, adversely affected person/entity); no administrative exhaustion required; relief includes injunctive, declaratory, compensatory damages, attorneys’ fees; abrogates state sovereign immunity.
- **Sec. 248:** No funds to finalize or implement proposed HHS rule “Nondiscrimination in Health Programs and Activities” (87 Fed. Reg. 47824, Aug 4, 2022) or similar.
- Cites title as “Department of Health and Human Services Appropriations Act, 2024”.

**TITLE III — DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION**

**Education for the Disadvantaged**
- $13,055,290,000 (Title I/II ESEA, HEA §418A); $2,126,990,000 available July 1, 2024–Sept 30, 2025; $10,841,177,000 available Oct 1, 2024–Sept 30, 2025. Specific allocations: $1,906,901,000 basic grants (§1124); $1,362,301,000 concentration grants (§1124A); $4,542,550,000 targeted grants (§1125); $4,542,550,000 education finance incentive grants (§1125A); $224,000,000 subpart 2 part B title II; $52,123,000 HEA §418A. Up to $5,000,000 for Census poverty data.

**Impact Aid**
- $1,618,112,000: $1,468,242,000 basic support (§7003(b)); $48,316,000 disabilities (§7003(d)); $18,406,000 construction (§7007(a)); $78,313,000 Federal property (§7002); $4,835,000 facilities maintenance (§7008). Special eligibility for children of deployed/deceased military parents residing on Federal property.

**School Improvement Programs**
- $4,850,428,000: $3,053,673,000 available July 1, 2024; $1,681,441,000 Oct 1, 2024. Includes $1,329,673,000 for Title IV-B; $45,897,000 Title VI-B (Native Hawaiian, construction allowed, 5% admin cap on direct costs); $44,953,000 Title VI-C (competitive, construction allowed); $24,464,000 Supplemental Education Grants (Micronesia/Marshall Islands, up to 5% for TA); $215,000,000 Title V-B; $1,380,000,000 Title IV-A subpart 1 (Secretary may reserve ≤1% for TA).

**Indian Education**
- $194,746,000: $72,000,000 subpart 2; $12,365,000 subpart 3. 5% admin cap on direct costs. Grants under §§6132/6133 may be up to 5 years.

**Innovation and Improvement**
- $737,000,000: $3,000,000 Title II-B subpart 3 (no regard to §§2201/2231(b)); $450,000,000 Title IV-C (no regard to §4311; §4303(d)(3)(A)(i) inapplicable); of IV-C, ≥$65,000,000 for §4304, ≤$140,000,000 for §4305(b) (available to March 31, 2025), ≤$16,000,000 for §4305(a)(3). Grantees under §4303 may use up to 10% for §4303(b)(2) and 5% for §4303(c)(1)(C). §4304(k) matching waived. $284,000,000 for Title IV-F subpart 1 (available to Dec 31, 2024).

**Safe Schools and Citizenship Education**
- $316,000,000 (available to Dec 31, 2024): $216,000,000 for §4631 (up to $5,000,000 Project SERV); $100,000,000 for §4625.

**Special Education**
- $15,453,264,000 (IDEA): $5,870,321,000 available July 1, 2024; $9,283,383,000 Oct 1, 2024. §611(b)(2) amount formula. Secretary distributes §612(a)(18)(B) reductions to other states (85% population, 15% poverty), excluding the reduced state. Reduction not considered in future base calculations. Secretary may spread reduction over ≤5 years; may proportionally reduce state reservation under §611(e)(1). §611(c) funds for data collection TA. State-level funds may be subgranted. §643(e) grants: if ≤5 states apply, each gets max; if >5, pro-rata by infant/toddler population capped at max. Part C funds may be subgranted; states may continue Part C services from age 3 until school year following third birthday.

**Rehabilitation Services**
- $4,397,033,000; $4,253,834,000 for Title I vocational rehabilitation grants.

**Special Institutions for Persons with Disabilities**
- American Printing House for the Blind: $43,431,000.
- National Technical Institute for the Deaf: $92,500,000; may use funds for endowment.
- Gallaudet University: $165,361,000; up to $15,000,000 for construction; may use funds for endowment.

**Career, Technical, and Adult Education**
- $2,191,436,000: $1,400,436,000 available July 1, 2024; $791,000,000 Oct 1, 2024. $25,000,000 for Perkins Act §114(e) innovation grants. $13,712,000 for AEFLA §242 national leadership.

**Student Financial Assistance**
- $22,475,352,000 (available through Sept 30, 2025). Maximum Pell Grant award year 2024-2025: $6,335.

**Student Aid Administration**
- $1,769,207,000 (available through Sept 30, 2025). Consolidation borrowers may select any servicer. New servicing environment must include multiple direct-contract servicers with performance-based allocation. Quarterly briefings on servicing contracts. Within 60 days, FSA spend plan for FY2024 with quarterly updates.

**Higher Education**
- $2,767,239,000 (HEA Titles III-VIII, Perkins §117). Title VI funds for foreign travel for national security language studies; up to 1% for evaluation/outreach. Up to 1.5% of Title IV-A subpart 2 chapter 2 for evaluation. HEA §313(d) inapplicable to §318-eligible institutions. ≥$10,000,000 for Title III-B grants to junior/community colleges (HEA §322(2)), allocated per §324.

**Howard University**
- $301,693,000; ≥$3,405,000 for matching endowment grant (until expended).

**College Housing and Academic Facilities Loans Program**
- $321,000 for administrative expenses.

**Historically Black College and University Capital Financing Program**
- $20,150,000 for loan costs (available through Sept 30, 2025); total loan principal up to $377,340,824; may support public/private HBCUs without regard to HEA §344(a) limits. $528,000 for administrative expenses.

**Institute of Education Sciences**
- $707,372,000 (available through Sept 30, 2025).

**Departmental Management**
- Program Administration: $350,000,000; non-career employee cap at Dec 31, 2021 level.
- Office for Civil Rights: $105,000,000.
- Office of Inspector General: $60,000,000; $3,000,000 available through Sept 30, 2025.

**General Provisions (TITLE III)**
- **Sec. 301:** No funds to prevent voluntary school prayer/meditation.
- **Sec. 302:** Up to 1% discretionary transfer authority; 3% increase cap; no new programs; 15-day notice.
- **Sec. 303:** ESEA §8601(c) evaluation funds available July 1, 2024–Sept 30, 2025.
- **Sec. 304:** HEA Title III/V endowment income usable for scholarships (subject to §331(c)(3)(B)(i)); prior use ratified; effective until reauthorization.
- **Sec. 305:** HEA §114(f) applied substituting “2024” for “2021”.
- **Sec. 306:** HEA §458(a)(4) applied substituting “2024” for “2021”.
- **Sec. 307:** Student Aid Administration funds may pay for Perkins Loan servicing by institutions.
- **Sec. 308:** Secretary may reserve ≤0.5% from HEA programs (excluding Pell) for evaluations; available through Sept 30, 2026; 30-day advance plan to Committees.
- **Sec. 309:** Up to $19,000,000 of IES for support services; Secretary may transfer excess/shortfall to/from Program Administration; 14-day notice.
- **Sec. 310:** Rescinds $29,000,000 from Education Nonrecurring Expenses Fund by Sept 30, 2024; Secretary may transfer up to $45,325,000 to Howard University hospital; restrictions on new obligations without prior notification.
- **Sec. 311:** No funds to finalize/implement Title IX proposed rules (87 Fed. Reg. 41390, July 12, 2022; 88 Fed. Reg. 22860, April 13, 2023) or similar athletic eligibility rules.
- **Sec. 312:** No funds to public IHEs denying religious student organizations rights/privileges afforded to other student organizations.
- **Sec. 313:** Rescinds $8,671,399,000 from Education for the Disadvantaged (FY2023 advance).
- **Sec. 314:** Rescinds $1,681,441,000 from School Improvement Programs (FY2023 advance).
- **Sec. 315:** No funds to implement student loan payment suspension extensions (87 Fed. Reg. 61513, Nov 22, 2022 announcement) or waive consequences of nonpayment.
- **Sec. 316:** No funds to implement debt discharge (87 Fed. Reg. 61514), finalize/implement income-driven repayment proposed rule (88 Fed. Reg. 1894), or implement/enforce borrower defense final rule (87 Fed. Reg. 65904) or similar actions.
- Cites title as “Department of Education Appropriations Act, 2024”.

**TITLE IV — RELATED AGENCIES**

**Committee for Purchase From People Who Are Blind or Severely Disabled**
- $13,124,000; requires written agreements with central nonprofit agencies containing auditing/oversight elements; no fee before agreement; ≥$3,150,000 for OIG.

**Corporation for National and Community Service**
- Operating Expenses: $593,347,000; up to 1% for grant review costs; local community need determination satisfies §122(c)(1)(D).
- Salaries and Expenses: $60,000,000.
- OIG: $7,595,000.
- **Sec. 401:** Significant changes only via notice-and-comment rulemaking; non-disclosure of grant selection information.
- **Sec. 402:** AmeriCorps minimum share 24% first 3 years, then per 45 CFR 2521.60, disregarding certain match limits.
- **Sec. 403:** Donations under 1990 Act §196 supplement not supplant.
- **Sec. 404:** Educational award use for veterans only (1990 Act §148(a)(4)).
- **Sec. 405:** 1990 Act §189D entities/individuals considered qualified entities/volunteers under NCPA; State Commissions may receive criminal history records.
- **Sec. 406:** 1,200-hour term in ≤1 year earns 70% of full education award.
- **Sec. 407:** Rescinds $243,000,000 from National Service Trust unobligated balances (excluding emergency-designated funds).

- $53,705,000; fees for training/arbitration credited to account, available until expended; arbitration fees only for workforce education/training; may accept gifts.

- $18,012,000.

- $294,800,000.

- $9,405,000.

- $13,824,000 (transferred from trust funds).

**National Council on Disability**
- $3,850,000.

**National Labor Relations Board**
- $200,000,000; no funds for organizing agricultural laborers.
- **Sec. 408:** No funds for electronic voting in representation elections.
- **Sec. 409:** No funds to alter/enforce “Joint Employer Status” final rule (86 Fed. Reg. 11184, Feb 26, 2020).

**National Mediation Board**
- $15,113,000.

**Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission**
- $15,449,000.

**Railroad Retirement Board**
- Dual Benefits: $8,000,000; up to 2% additional if needed; credited monthly.
- Federal Payments to Railroad Retirement Accounts: $150,000 (available through Sept 30, 2025).
- Limitation on Administration: $103,000,000; attorneys via excepted service; students/recent graduates via excepted hiring authorities.

**Social Security Administration**
- Payments to Trust Funds: $10,000,000.
- SSI: $45,455,426,000 (until expended); unspent state funds return to Treasury; ≤$91,000,000 for research (available through Sept 30, 2026); such sums for post-June 15 benefits; $21,700,000,000 for Q1 FY2025 benefits.
- Limitation on Administrative Expenses: ≤$11,951,978,000; ≥$2,700,000 for Advisory Board; unobligated balances available for IT infrastructure; reimbursement for union official time/facilities. Additional $1,851,000,000 for CDRs/redeterminations/anti-fraud (available through March 31, 2025); $273,000,000 meets BBEDCA §251(b)(2)(B)(ii)(III); $1,578,000,000 new budget authority; up to $18,000,000 transferable to OIG for CDI units; annual report required. $150,000,000 from SSI admin fees >$5.00 (until expended). **TITLE V — GENERAL PROVISIONS**
- **Sec. 501:** Transfer of unexpended prior balances to corresponding current accounts.
- **Sec. 502:** Funds available only for current fiscal year unless expressly provided.
- **Sec. 503:** Prohibits publicity/propaganda, lobbying with appropriations; includes advocacy on tax increases, consumer product restrictions, gun control.
- **Sec. 504:** Official reception/representation expense caps: Labor $28,000; Education $20,000; FMCS $5,000; NMB $5,000.
- **Sec. 505:** Grantees must disclose federal/non-federal cost percentages and dollar amounts in public documents.
- **Sec. 506:** No funds for abortion or health benefits coverage including abortion.
- **Sec. 507:** Exceptions for rape/incest/life endangerment; does not prohibit state/local/private funds; protects health care entities from discrimination for refusing abortion.
- **Sec. 508:** No funds for human embryo creation for research or destructive embryo research.
- **Sec. 509:** No funds to promote legalization of Schedule I drugs (except therapeutic advantage/clinical trials).
- **Sec. 510:** No funds for unique health identifier standard until legislation enacted.
- **Sec. 511:** No contracts with entities failing to submit veteran employment reports (38 U.S.C. 4212).
- **Sec. 512:** No transfers outside this Act’s authority.
- **Sec. 513:** LSTA funds conditioned on CIPA certifications.
- **Sec. 514:** Reprogramming restrictions; 15-day consultation/10-day notice for specified actions.
- **Sec. 515:** No political disclosure for scientific advisory candidates; no deliberately false/misleading information.
- **Sec. 516:** 45-day operating plan for deviations from Act/committee report/budget request.
- **Sec. 517:** Quarterly report on non-competitive contracts/grants >$500,000.
- **Sec. 518:** No processing of Social Security credit claims based on another’s SSN used in a conviction.
- **Sec. 519:** No funds for totalization agreement with Mexico.
- **Sec. 520:** Computer networks must block pornography; exception for law enforcement.
- **Sec. 521:** HHS divisions considered independent agencies for conference spending rules; scientific conferences tabulated separately.
- **Sec. 522:** Federal advertising must state taxpayer funding.
- **Sec. 523:** Up to 10 Performance Partnership Pilots (authority extended to Sept 30, 2028); includes communities with civil unrest; existing pilots may get 5-year extension.
- **Sec. 524:** Quarterly reports on balances of appropriations, identifying source years from FY2012.
- **Sec. 525:** 3 business days’ advance notice of discretionary grant awards.
- **Sec. 526:** No funds for sterile needles/syringes except if local health department determines HIV/hepatitis outbreak risk and program complies with state/local law.
- **Sec. 527:** 45 business days to answer congressional questions; $1,000/day rescission from specified accounts for noncompliance.
- **Sec. 528:** $13,493,000,000 in Child Enrollment Contingency Fund not available for obligation.
